title: Armstrong's singing, his playing and what it was like working with him
summary: Armstrong played the way he sang; playing with him every night was a ball, and he was a down-home man, not a distant leader.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, Louie -- it's been pointed out many times that Louie -- usually it says that Louie sang the way he played, but what you're saying really is, he played the way he sang. The other way around.
Yeah. Louie -- I don't know -- that really was something else. He didn't have a beautiful voice, but there was something in it that you would like and I've been trying to find out what was it.

I just liked to hear him. Now, you take -- you say -- let's see, "Hello, Dolly, looking swell, Dolly," and the way he -- the idiom and the way he would carry the tune, you couldn't help but to make you sit there and pat your foot.
And he's singing and laughing all --
That must have been a great inspiration playing with him every night for all those years.
Yeah, oh, yeah, every night. We had a ball.
Was he one of the guys or was he like some of the leaders and sort of, you know, didn't mix with the guys too much?
No, no, he wasn't that kind. No --
A very down-home type of guy.
He was a very kind man. He was very kind to me when I was quite young.
